paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption_used: Sparsity ratio of SDPA output across layers under the 1e-2 threshold, comparing three gating configurations. The sparsity ratio before gate (blue dashed, avg 0.03) begins at approximately 0.2 and declines steadily to near zero by layer 5, remaining flat thereafter. The sparsity ratio after gate (orange dotted, avg 0.44) starts at 1.0 and decreases sharply, converging with the after-average-gate line near 0.15 by layer 10 before both stabilize. Notably, the after-average-gate configuration (green dash-dot, avg 0.33) consistently maintains higher sparsity than the after-gate line across all layers beyond the initial decline, with the two lines never intersecting after layer 5. The before-gate configuration demonstrates that pre-gating hidden states exhibit minimal sparsity throughout the network.

model_annotations.German: The diagram illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output as a function of the layer number for three different gating configurations: before gate, after gate, and after average gate. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," ranges from 0 to 25 and is divided into equal intervals. The y-axis is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also divided into equal intervals. The "before gate" line is represented by a blue dashed line, the "after gate" by an orange dotted line, and the "after average gate" by a green dash-dot line. The values on the x-axis are not explicitly marked, but the graph provides a visual representation of the trends. The "before gate" line starts at approximately 0.2, decreases steadily, and flattens out as it approaches layer 5. The "after gate" line begins at 1.0 and drops sharply, converging with the "after average gate" line near 0.15 by layer 10. The "after average gate" line starts higher than the other two, around 0.75, and maintains a higher sparsity ratio than the "after gate" throughout the rest of the layers. The lines do not intersect after layer 5. This chart does not include any annotations for specific data points, peaks, troughs, or trends beyond the general pattern indicated by the graph.
